description:
The Interactive Agricultural and Folklore Museum of Varnavas explores rural and domestic life in Attica. Its collections bring together objects used in the home, farming and traditional crafts.

Costumes, textiles, embroidery, lamps, household utensils and agricultural tools document changing ways of life. Historical archives, books and craft workshops connect material objects with the knowledge and practices behind them.

description:
The Jewish Museum of Greece in Athens was founded in 1977 to preserve the heritage of Greek Jewish communities. Early collecting brought together religious objects, historical documents and personal possessions.

Liturgical textiles, books and domestic material illuminate the lives and traditions of these communities. The museum’s history also connects the collections with wartime loss, survival and the preservation of memory.

description:
The Faltaits Museum in Skyros was founded by Manos Faltaits in 1964. Its historic mansion setting houses collections concerned with the island’s daily life, traditions and wider Greek folk culture.

description:

description:
The museum within Chlemoutsi Castle explores the period of Frankish rule in Greece. The thirteenth-century fortress and palace provides a historic setting for collections concerning the medieval Morea.

Architectural fragments, sculpture, pottery, coins, frescoes and personal objects date chiefly from the thirteenth to fifteenth centuries. Much of the material comes from excavations in Elis and the wider Principality of Achaea.

description:

description:
The National Historical Museum in Athens was established in 1884 by the Historical and Ethnological Society of Greece. It is housed in the Old Parliament building on Stadiou Street.

Weapons, relics, memorabilia and works of art are supported by historical, photographic and film archives. Research and conservation connect these objects with the people, events and experiences represented in the museum.
